scope.out_of_scope: mythic: needs new geometry (sleeved light jersey, belt, front drape) and is built elsewhere with the Meshy API. Not read, not measured, not in any table of this report.

method.family_convention: a = larger cluster (dominant garment mass), b = trim

heuristics.skin: hue 9-38 deg and sat > 0.30 (declared port heuristic) AND val > 0.50 (MEASURED floor for this athlete: the declared skin #b06a3f has val p10 0.60-0.61 over the six sheets, the leather mass 0.03-0.35, and the bare hue+sat rule alone would remove 61.6-66.3% of the body)
heuristics.racket: geometric: inside each band, the body's own column block is the run of columns whose occupancy is >= 0.85 of the band height; ink left of it, separated by a fully transparent column gap of >= 3 px, is the racket. The Maestro's gold-blob rule does NOT apply here: the bright-gold family is 0.00-0.89% of the body and its largest blob is 8-46 px, because this racket's head is black and its frame is dark brass.

hem_detection.note: the shorts hem is the row where the silhouette's widest run drops below 62%% of the previous row's: below the hem the figure splits into two narrow legs. This is what sets the hip band's bottom edge.

notes: the atlas has ONE saturated hue family: the saturated bands are 0-30 deg and 30-60 deg and there is nothing else above 1%%. Skin, the brass trim and the emissive orange all live in that band, so a hue-based family test cannot separate two garment families on this athlete the way it does on Fiamma.

the dark leather mass is largely BELOW the shader's sat_min: only the share reported in dark_texels_passing_family_test survives the family test, so the `a` slots of a profile anchored on that leather risk being inert.

atlas_family_split_in_mask.note: the family test is run on the BAKED ATLAS TEXEL, not on the target colour, so a target that is dark or desaturated is NOT inert: the shader still recolours the texel. What makes a slot inert is the ANCHOR failing the test, and what makes a recolour invisible is the TARGET sitting on top of its own baked anchor (see target_vs_baked_anchor).

cross_check_mask_lane_hue_window.note: the mask lane's figure is a pure hue-window count and this reproduction agrees with it to within about a percent; the shader's smoothstep ramps reject a further ~25 points of that set, and THAT is the count the render actually sees. The residual difference is the mask revision: this tool reads whatever mask is on disk when it runs.

region_change_delta.note: shares of the region's own opaque pixels (alpha > 200); the two sheets are different resolutions and are NEVER resampled against each other here.

metal_map_inventory.note: read-only inventory; it does not enter any slot value. The map is a different resolution from the colour atlas, so it cannot be indexed against it here without a resample, which this tool refuses to do silently.

glb_texture_check.note: the GLB's embedded images are compared by sha256 prefix with the shipped colosso_texture_0.png: a match means the atlas measured above is the one the rig renders.

card_check.note: a card that differs from the base card over most of its area is a different illustration, not a recolour; the in-field sprite is the reference for this document. Resampled numbers are labelled as such: comparing two different resolutions produces a percentage that is mostly a resampling artefact and is not quoted as a result.

sheet_bleed.note: columns belonging to a neighbouring figure's ink; excluded from the colour measurement

racket_rule_gold_blob_check.note: the Maestro's racket rule (largest bright-gold blob) is only usable if the blob is actually the racket. On Colosso the racket head is black and its frame is dark brass, so the bright-gold family is expected to be near-empty; this is the measurement behind that expectation, and it is why racket_columns() is geometric.

risk_orange_vs_skin_hue.note: the glow and the skin are the same hue band on this athlete. The value floor that removes the leather from the skin rule also removes the glow, because the glow is the brightest warm thing in the sprite. Value is the only lever available and it is the same lever.
